learning_outcomes.description: Identify and discuss the roles, responsibilities and contributions of pharmacists in society.
Apply foundational concepts in chemistry that are important for understanding the action of drugs.
Apply the foundational principles of drug therapy, drug delivery, dose form design, compounding and pharmaceutical calculations in a pharmacy practice context.
Describe processes and regulations regarding medicines in the Australian health system.
Collaborate effectively with colleagues to make informed team decisions and demonstrate communication skills.
Develop patient-centred care strategies such as respect, building rapport, and attentiveness to patients' specific needs.
Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating information from reputable sources; interpreting evidence, and making and justifying inferences and judgments.
Reflect on your development as a health professional to identify gaps in and challenges to your learning.

assessments.task_description:
These engagement activities are associated with the Pharmacy Practice Modules in PHRM1101. Students will work collaboratively in teams to complete these activities. Each team will be allocated a team number and a private Microsoft Teams channel for communication and submission of contributions.

  • Team Intro Post (1%): Students will collaboratively create a Team Charter , post it in their team's private channel, and each member will provide a response.
  • Info Source Activity (1%): Students will use the Pharmacy Information Source Tool to answer BINGO questions by posting responses in their team's private channel.
  • Ethics & Discussions (3%): Students will engage with their team in two ethics tasks and one patient-centred care (PCC) task, contributing an individual argument and responding to a teammate within their private channel while exploring key ethical issues in pharmacy practice, comparing approaches to PCC, and developing well-reasoned arguments.

These engagement activities are assessed based on individual contributions within the team. Further details for each activity will be provided in advance on Learn.UQ (Blackboard) and UQ Extend prior to commencement.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Each team will have a private Microsoft Teams channels. All engagement activities will be completed within this channel, including uploading files, contributing to the shared documents, and posting comments or replies where applicable.

assessments.task_description:
• This group assessment provides students with an opportunity to develop and demonstrate their ability to communicate complex pharmaceutical and health information to patients in a clear, accurate, and accessible manner.
  • Students will work in their allocated teams to create a short educational video and an accompanying patient information leaflet on an assigned topic. All team members are required to contribute meaningfully to the assessment and appear and speak in the video.
  • The assessment consists of a video of up to three minutes and a one-page information leaflet written in plain language to complement and reinforce the key messages presented in the video.
  • Students are required to use evidence-based information and APA 7th referencing, with references included in both the video and leaflet.
  • The assessment will be marked as a group submission, and further details, assessment requirements, and marking criteria will be provided on Learn.UQ (Blackboard).


Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) requirements

  • Permitted use: Generative AI tools may be used to support brainstorming, planning, content organisation, language refinement, and grammar checking. AI must not replace the group’s own understanding, evaluation of evidence, scientific reasoning, or professional judgement. The group remains responsible for the originality, accuracy, appropriateness, and final wording of all submitted content. Any information produced or suggested by AI must be independently checked against credible sources.
  • Academic integrity requirements: AI use must comply with UQ’s academic integrity requirements and remain within the permitted purposes described above. Unacknowledged or inappropriate AI use, including the submission of inaccurate, fabricated, or misleading content, may constitute academic misconduct.
  • AI acknowledgement: All generative AI use must be acknowledged. The acknowledgement must identify the tool used and briefly describe how it contributed to the work. Groups must retain relevant prompts and AI-generated outputs and provide these records if requested. If no generative AI was used, this must also be declared. Examples of acceptable AI acknowledgement statements will be provided on Learn.UQ (Blackboard).

assessments.task_description:
The Objective Structured Clinical Exam (OSCE) is an individual assessment designed to evaluate students' ability to communicate effectively with patients in a pharmacy context while demonstrating patient-centred care.

  • Students will complete a 5-minute face-to-face oral consultation with an examiner acting as a patient at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences.
  • Students must arrive before the start of the session to sign in with their student ID. Students will remain in a holding room until they are called for their examination, and may leave once their examination has concluded.
  • The OSCE is a closed-book assessment. Students are not permitted to bring any materials into the examination. This includes, but is not limited to, pens, calculators, notes, textbooks, phones, computers, tablets, etc.
  • The OSCE will be audio-recorded and retained as per university policy for purposes of moderation, feedback, and approved re-marking processes.
  • This assessment must be completed in person. The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is not permitted.
  • Further details, assessment requirements, and marking criteria will be provided on Learn.UQ (Blackboard).
  • The grade for this assessment may also be used to identify students who could benefit from a free English language support course offered in the subsequent semester.
assessments.submission_guidelines: The OSCE will be performed in person at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences in an exam slot timetabled by the school (EXM1).

assessments.task_description:
Reflection is an essential skill for health professionals, enabling continuous evaluation of clinical experience, identification of learning needs, and improvement of future professional practice.

Following the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), students are required to complete an individual reflection on their OSCE experience, including their performance, strengths, areas for improvement, and strategies for future development.

Students will use the PHRM1101 OSCE Reflection Builder, available on Blackboard, to enter their OSCE results and prepare a structured reflection using the 4Rs reflective framework (Report and Respond, Relate, Reason, and Reconstruction). The tool will generate a single-slide reflection summary as a PDF, which students must submit as first assessment component.

For the second component, students will record a two-minute video reflection, verbally expanding on the content of their generated slide. The recording should discuss their OSCE performance, factors influencing their experience, key learning, and specific strategies for future improvement. Students are not required to display the slide during the recording.

This exam will assess you on the pharmaceutical science content of PHRM1101 that includes Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry, and Drug Delivery. The exam will require you to demonstrate and apply your content knowledge in the context of an allocated drug.

  • This is a CLOSED-BOOK, on-campus invigilated exam.
  • Students will be completing and submitting the exam using their own device (laptop).
  • The exam will be undertaken via the Inspera eAssessment platform. Go to the Inspera Assessment Information page to navigate to the Library Services web page which provides further information on: how to access Inspera, on-campus invigilated exams in Inspera, device requirements, familiarisation opportunities, submitting assessment and access to the Student Laptop Scheme and short-term laptop-loans.
  • The exam may contain a mixture of question types including multiple choice questions (MCQ), multiple response questions, matching/pairing, calculations, hotspot, drag and drop, graphic matching, and short answer questions (SAQs). 
  • The questions will assess content from UQ Extend, Seminars, Workshops, Practicals and online quiz questions.
